t: Kill the Prophetic Cobra and thrust the Spear of Truth into its flesh.

A spear base is ready. A good and strong spear it would be, but only for the enemy with the flesh. Truth, inscribed on the spear, needs a witness. Mighty, valorous, wise. Do you know which animal knows all the truth, the whole story of world's birth to this day? A snake! But not any snake, no.
Find an old cobra, Prophetic Cobra. Defeat it in a battle. Thrust the spear into the cobra's flesh - a spirit will move into the spear and confirm every truth inscribed on it. Then the spear will gain power!
Truth is helpless against lies if there is no witness!
I witness-s-s-s... There is-s-s truth written on this-s-s-s s-s-s-spear, truth-th-th-th...
Kill the Prophetic Cobra and thrust the Spear of Truth into its flesh.

Discuss the plan of opposing Tep with Klavdia and speak with Cha Pie-Pie.

Tep doesn't expect any trouble from the League or the Empire. He thinks he's all-powerful; for him, you, me and other "bugs" are ignorable, yet a bit annoying misunderstanding! It's time to show him the difference between arrogance and true faith in oneself. Let's quickly review the plan of action and get on with it. Cha Pie-Pie needs your help. We'll play fair, and this would be against Tep's expectations!
What a mess! This is anarchy! Where is everyone? How can you fight like this?
Ah, there you are! This is a decisive, fateful moment, and you just went absent without official leave? For shame!
You are going to ruin us!
Discuss the plan of opposing Tep with Klavdia and speak with Ko'Chak.

Tep doesn't expect any trouble from the League or the Empire. He thinks he's all-powerful; for him, you, me and other "bugs" are ignorable, yet a bit annoying misunderstanding! It's time to show him the difference between arrogance and true faith in oneself. Let's quickly review the plan of action and get on with it. Ko'Chak needs your help. We'll play fair, and this would be against Tep's expectations!
This is a hard time. A time to be decisive or die.
Son of the Wind! Where were you? White-wings' mission needs your help more than ever!
Find Crow the Riverborn near the Snake Waterfalls.

Where were you? Why did you leave without commander permission? Where did you go? Drinking? You should be shot, you bastard! The situation is hard enough without you acting like little devils! Causing trouble for Cha Pie-Pie!
OK, OK, don't be angry, I lose my temper there for a minute. You see the situation on the front. Chaos, apathy, morale's six feet underground... I caught one soldier so drunk his feathers were falling off. He said he wanted to live a little before attack. Can you believe? He wanted to live, not fight!
What attack? You should have listened to the commander, even if you have no wings. The Steel Claw tribe prepares to attack Windy Hills. The Empire helps them build small foothold, most forces follow behind.
You must stop hang around here with nothing to do. Go and join vanguard. Wingless one can use a lift near the Snake Waterfalls. It's guarded by a big wingless, called Crow the Riverborn, he'll show you the way. Don't lose courage! If you die, the red-wing army will avenge you!
Yo, homie! Things around here are lousy as ever.
Find the elevator near the Sunny Cascade.

Bad news, Son of the Wind - villages burn again, blood is spilt on the dry ground. A wounded messenger has just come. The Steel Claw tribe on Windy Hills got brazen, attacked our settlements! Why? There's no secret, kerpa-mar-rua! They have a new ally! Two legs, no feathers, just like you. It's the Empire!
You know the Empire, you've fought and beaten them many times. Let me ask you, Son of the Wind, to stand for truth again. The Glittering Wing tribe will die but never surrender. You must save them! Hurry up, help my brothers beat red-bellied scoundrels!
Your squawker does not know the road to Hills, but even wingless one can get there. We've build a wonderful device near Sunny Cascade, a machine to move you up with no wings! It carries big and heavy load, so it will easily carry you. Son of the Wind, please hurry. Remember, one who protects his feathers will lose his honor!
We didn't touch anything! It did it by itself!
What do we do? We just can't start climbing these rocks, you know! Where is that aviak?
Obtain 5 components of mosaic map by fighting stone elementals in the mine and repair the mysterious mechanism.

There is an ancient mechanism hiding by the wall. It's not damaged, but it doesn't respond when you pull its lever, kick or curse at it. Its stone sides were once decorated with mosaics. If you wipe off the century-old dust, you can still see tiny smalt slabs which come together in a peculiar picture. It's not a landscape or a portrait, or even an abstract image. It's... a magical symbol! Perhaps the machine will regain functionality if the mosaic is restored?
On the floor underneath the machine there is only garbage, but a closer look at the stone elementals roaming the mine reveals shiny slabs on the chests of some of them. If you take apart five or so, you'll have enough pieces to restore the symbol and try to activate the mechanism.
This is but a strange lever on a mysterious mechanism in an ancient mine, built by a now-extinct race many eons ago. What could go wrong if you press it?

Almost all the slabs have returned to their place. Something roars inside the mechanism, as the mosaic begins to radiate a soft inner light in the twilight. From deep within the bowels of the mine comes an answer, as the crystal resting atop a large stone tablet lights up in return. Could that be a door? What could it be hiding?
Discover what is hidden behind the door in the mine and report to Semer Nifuni at the Imperial Outpost.

You have fixed the mechanism. Now you just have to pull the lever and open the door that leads to... What? Treasures? Secret knowledge? Ancient monsters? Or, perhaps, nothing but dust and cobwebs? There is only one way to find out, that is to enter.
An ancient mine? A sealed door? What was behind it? Oh, you didn't open it... Well, I can only commend your wisdom.

A new archeological find? Where is this coming from? Oh, a strange mechanism and a door that leads into an ancient burial chamber... Did you ever think that pulling every lever you came across would sooner or later drop something heavy on your head?
Discover what is hidden behind the door in the mine and report to Bogomil Svetlov in the League Settlement.

You have fixed the mechanism. Now you just have to pull the lever and open the door that leads to... What? Treasures? Secret knowledge? Ancient monsters? Or, perhaps, nothing but dust and cobwebs? There is only one way to find out, that is to enter.
A sealed door in the June mine? It could be dangerous... But Tensess honors the brave! Go and open it with my blessing!
There is an unknown allod that contains an ancient mine, and in that mine there is a mysterious door... It is a riddle wrapped in an enigma! Well, what did you find?
Show the ancient amulet to Mage Zayan in Avilon.

I am no expert in art history, but I can definitely tell you that this doesn't look like either June or elven or any other traditional art that's taught in colleges. However, as an expert in magic technology, I can definitely tell you that this talisman is harmless and presents purely historical interest. You can do anything you like with it, but I would recommend consulting with the Historians. You know Zayan, don't you? An expert of his caliber will certainly be able to at least identify the culture that produced this artifact.

Let's see here... You know, I'm ashamed to admit it, but I've never seen anything like this in my life. Are you sure it's not a replica? These days there are many people who like to profit from falsifying history. For instance, we recently had a scandal with "historical finds" on Asee-Teph. The League and the Empire were simultaneously caught red-handed forging finds - there was a huge scandal... So, where did this little trinket come from?
A sealed tomb in an illusory world, eh?... Hmm, perhaps this amulet is also somebody's fantasy? To be honest, it's easier for me to believe in the materialization of dreams - yours, Tep's, the aviaks' - than in an entire culture somehow escaping the Historians' attention, aside from a single lonely artifact.
On the other hand, the Irdrich Allod really did exist, it really was populated by the aviak race, and they really did war with one another. Perhaps the illusory copy of this allod is precise enough to supply historically valuable evidence?
Let's do this. I'll keep the amulet and will try to find out more about it. An entire civilization could not have vanished without a trace. I'll write to you if I learn anything. In the meantime, this beauty will add to my collection of curiosities...
Show the ancient amulet to Mage Zayan in Avilon.

What an extraordinary thing... Just look at this engraving! It doesn't look like Elven craftsmanship... definitely not Zem... and it certainly has nothing in common with Junes! I doubt anyone in our expedition team can explain the origins of this amulet.
Have you been to Avilon? Go there and show the amulet to the Historians. They'll know for sure where it came from.

Find 6 Dead Scouts in the gorge, use the Ice Sarcophagus scroll on them and report to Celestine de Desirae.

Are you looking to cross to the other side of the gorge? My detachment was looking for it, too. As was the Imperial detachment, it turned out. When we ran into each other, we put aside our geographical research and charged into battle. In the heat of it, a third party decided to join us - wild crawlers! Sadly, the outcome was quite predictable: the only survivors were myself and mister... No, check that, Comrade Anokh! We still haven't found a way across, but our friends and comrades... Oh, you must help us!
The crawlers took their bodies with them. I can't imagine what they will do with them! Please, find our dead companions and protect them against defilement until they resurrect. And please protect the Imperials as well: some things are above faction rivalries. Here's an Ice Sarcophagus scroll - it will protect the bodies from wild animals and other local horrors.
We alternate fighting amongst ourselves, then against a common enemy, then amongst ourselves again... I must admit that I'm completely confused and no longer understand who is on whose side.
Oh, thank you! I hope that they have stocked up on mirra and will soon resurrect. I don't feel very comfortable in this picturesque spot.
Kill 12 crawlers (workers or warriors) and their Queen in the Gorge. Report your success to Sarbaz Anokh.

The Ice Sarcophaguses of Mademoiselle de Desirae are quite good. However, I'd suggest that you protect the bodies of our friends and enemies in a different way. We the Arisen are quiet proficient in the matter. I'll paraphrase an old saying for you: "Bodies are safe not where they are being guarded, but where there isn't anyone around to eat them." And if there's nobody around to make new dead bodies, even better. You get my drift?
It seems that we've stirred up the crawlers' nest. Pacifying them won't work, so you'll just have to kill them. And don't forget their queen, lest the entire swarm will be here soon.

You've no idea what it's like to wake up from an aeon-long sleep and discover that your face has been devoured by insects. I wouldn't wish that upon my worst enemy, not even an Elf... Oh, Mademoiselle de Desirae, I do apologize!
Did you exterminate the pests? My thanks. Now we just need to wait for our warriors' resurrection... And hope that they won't send each other back to the Purgatory.
Find Fragments of June Golem on the bottom of the Gorge and bring them to Celestine de Desirae.

You've also heard old Ulumi's story, haven't you? What a dreadful fate - to lose one's friends, become a cripple, an outcast... and all of it over one courageous impulse... Anyway, let's not talk about sad things. There was one small detail in his story that I found curious. Do you remember how the part about overcoming one of the statues and casting it into the abyss? How would you like to see it? I, for one, would like that very much. In fact, I bet that it will be our old friends, June golems! Would it be too much to ask you to find that statue and bring me a few pieces?
I suppose I could do it myself... but what if my friends resurrect and start looking for me here? It would be so frustrating to get lost, on top of that all!
I have discovered something very interesting. Obviously, not without help from my Imperial... ahem... colleague.

Che-Go is my highly revered ancestor, that is my grandpa. He's gotten quite old, you see, so he's not all there. Then again, he would say the same exact thing back when he was younger and I was just a child. He used to make me memorize all kinds of dusty legends and clean this old statue... What, you want to know about the crocodile as well? Fine, you asked for it.
But if I lose my place or mess up, don't tell grandpa, OK?
So that's the legend. Of course, no one has ever seen this divine croc with their own eyes. Whereas the Immortals are frequent visitors! So can you blame me for doubting these old wives' tales?
Tell Yasskul Tikhti at the Imperial Outpost about the golem pieces found on the bottom of the gorge.

Mademoiselle de Desirae and I have carefully studied the pieces and have discovered something interesting. Do you see these long lines, cut in stone? They are a kind of instructions, left for the golem by its creator. In spite of my Elvish colleague's earnest attempts to assist, I was able to decipher them. The orders left for the golem were very simple - don't let any aerial target pass. Do you understand what that means? The residents of the island, whoever they were, knew about aviaks and didn't want to have anything to do with them.
I don't think that we will find anything useful in the gorge, but Mademoiselle de Desirae is simply radiating enthusiasm. I guess the only thing I can do is wait for my buddies to resurrect and search this gorge again for any secret trails that lead to the top. While you should go back to ours and report about the golems. As we have discovered, the taboo on flights to the Crystal Mountain is substantiated.
June golems? What's next, Wormfaces? Or perhaps the illusory world has preserved the Junes as they were before the curse? It's getting more and more curious...
Tell the Pudgy Family at the League Settlement about the golem pieces found on the bottom of the gorge.

Just be grateful for my intelligence, knowledge and experience, and also for my colleague's quick wit! We have discovered something very interesting. Do you see these signs on the cogwheels? They are actually commands, left by the golem's creators for him to follow. So, what do you think they ordered him to do? Fine, fine, I won't tease you. But imagine... the golem was placed there with but a single goal: never let anything with wings pass by him. In other words, there is someone there who knows about aviaks and doesn't wish to see them.
This means that we will not be able to fly across. I'm glad that we discovered this before flying here on squawkers. Return to the Settlement and tell your contacts about this find. We'll wait until the fallen are resurrected and start looking for a path from the bottom of the gorge. I am certain that there must be some convenient trail or a secret cave there!

So, that's the scoop. Golems won't let anyone pass, not even a fly or a bird. What a pity... and we were about to build a glider. What if we try to catapult you in? Or use a large slingshot? What do you say to that?
It's been almost a century since my name day, but I have never met creatures like yourself.

What a delicate taste and flavor! I...What's going on? I start... recalling!
O, the Ancients! O, glorious Genlun! Forgive us, your imprudent children! What a shame...

Take a look around. What you see before you is Tequatl - the only settlement of our ancient nation. Its beauty rivals that of mandarin flowers in spring, though it cannot compare with the beauty of a city on the ruins of which it was built and whose name it bears.
Tequatl was the city of the Ancients. They were all-knowing, all-powerful and wielded great magic. The Ancients knew how to make rock come alive. They were masters of the heavens and the earth. Our small nation was like a younger sibling to them, and we lived our lives without worry. Only vague legends remain of those wonderful times.
The Ancients had a sworn enemy. A monster from the Void which cannot be described: even the words are scared of him and fall to silence. Who he was and where he came from is beyond our grasp. The Enemy was so powerful that all of the Ancients' wisdom and magic wasn't enough to protect them. Before they perished, in their dying moments the Ancients made sure to save us, their children and heirs. We have built our own Tequatl on the ruins of the great Tequatl of the Ancients. Thus began a new era for my people - an era of darkness and solitude. We dug roots and hunted mice, learned to build fires and sew simple rough garments for wear. Long were those days, and filled with sorrow. So thunderous was the Tekyans' cry of despair that the world split into two!
But everything changed when They came. The true gods appeared to our people. They have built their palace on the mountain and settled there. They taught our people to build houses, sew beautiful clothing from soft fabrics, and cook delicious food. And all they asked in return was our devotion. The gods are powerful, righteous and kind. And if you prove your faith, you too may experience their favor!
h: Ask the sage about the Tekyan people

t: Obtain 10 Leopard Claws and 6 Leopard Skins and bring them to Ulumi Half-Wing in the Muggy Jungle.

There was a time when I was strong and brave. But now I'm a cripple and I'm stupid, cough, cough... All I can do is to collect berries and nuts, catch mice and dig roots. I can also make a cape, but I have no material. Help an old man, bring me leopard skins and claws. I'll make a good cape, and trade it for wine and meat... Kha-kharrr...
I can't even hunt anymore. Clearly, I will die soon. A preacher came to me, he promised eternal life and Light... Kharr... What kind of life is that, especially if eternal...
I thank you, wingless one, you helped an old man. Maybe someone will give me some hot food for this cape. Kharr! I'm so sick of the roots' taste...

I don't even know whom to believe - grandpa with his sacred crocodiles, or everyone else with the Immortals. May the grass be like silk under their feet and oranges sweet in their mouths, I just want them to leave me alone. I am but a humble Tekyan - who am I to pass judgments on gods? Give me a cup of hot tea and a good haul of fish, and I'm happy. As far as tea goes, I have plenty of it, so come by and have a cup. Fish, however, is a different story. See all those crocodiles in the river? Grandpa can worship them from morning till night if he wants, but I'm not going anywhere near that river.
Listen, can you chase them off while grandpa's not looking? I just need some space to fish in peace. I'll give you tea and fish and oranges...
Who are you and where did you come from? Irdrich hasn't seen creatures like you in centuries!
For shame, mortal, for shame! You are a guest on Irdrich, and look what you are doing... Killing crocodiles, my kin!
Jump over the abyss and make contact with the inhabitants of the Crystal Mountain.

You know... It would seem like all our efforts have been wasted. But that's not the case. The illusion is still strong, but we are already beginning to undermine it. It's not just that there are holes in the illusory reality, I've also noticed several places where one's will and intellect are capable of overriding the laws of the imaginary world! With confidence strong enough, in such places one can stand on air and manipulate the patterns of falling leaves - all without any magic at all. Is your confidence strong?
Don't worry, my friend, you are not in any danger. But remember - everything around us is an illusion. It must obey your mind, not the other way around. If you keep that in mind, a properly timed and executed running jump should allow you to leap over the abyss in one go!
Who else walks our sacred ground, our reed valley? Did someone call you to the Crystal Mountain, the blessed island?
Jump over the abyss and make contact with the inhabitants of the Crystal Mountain.

You know, we've noticed... Our efforts were not fruitless. Bit by bit, the illusion is beginning to crumble. It's not just the holes in it - we've found places where the laws of this world no longer have power. In these places, you can levitate by the force of your will. Or turn a mug upside down in a way that nothing pours out of it. Or you can light or extinguish fire without any magic. Can you imagine?
Hey, I have an idea! Feeling weak in the knees? Relax! Let me explain. All you need is to believe in yourself and jump. You don't have wings, so golems won't even notice you. Isn't that awesome? Pow, and you're on the other side!
Come on, don't be stubborn, this is our only option. Be confident and remember that the illusion must obey your mind, and not the other way around, and then... Then you jump!
Who else walks our sacred ground, our reed valley? Did someone call you to the Crystal Mountain, the blessed island?
Bring Genlun's Tooth to Tequatl and show it to its inhabitants.

Very well, I accept your apology. Now, dear guest, shall we talk? I'm so tired of feeling lonely.
There was a time, long long ago, when I used to care for the Tekyans, and they loved me in return... I never needed any other sacrifice. They didn't dare touch crocodiles, and the crocodiles didn't touch them. Now everything has changed - only old Che-Go remembers me. The rest of the Tekyans kill crocodiles; in return, my babies feast on them at every opportunity. But the scary part is not that the Tekyans have forgotten me. It's that they have forgotten themselves.
Whose fault is that? I think you already know. The "Immortals." I don't know who they are or where they came from, but I do know WHAT they are. They are a fraud, deceit and deception. Everything they touch turns to sham. Sometimes I think that Irdrich itself... No, I don't even want to think about that.
I can see that you have a strong will and a clear mind. Lies have no hold over you. Let's try to help the Tekyans return back to their roots. Take my tooth. Return to Tequatl and raise it above you head, and then... Then you'll see what happens next.
How do you like the statue of our god? What elegance, what stature! There is simply no comparison with that ugly idol.
Genlun has returned, Genlun has returned! Now everything will change, you'll see.. That is, change back to the way it was... But not in the same way it is right now, yeah!
Find and break the next knot of illusory web.

That was simply amazing. I don't know where you find crocodiles like this, but I hope there are a couple more left. You just can't imagine what happened in the real world. An entire knot burned up like a feather!
What's a knot? Oh yeah, you don't know... In short, the Resistance has been digging at the inner structure of the illusory world and found something interesting. The illusion is constructed like a web, and its knots are both the most important and most vulnerable places. And one of those knots simply ceased to exist when your sacred crocodile returned from oblivion - it literally burned out. The knots hinge on a steady sequence of events, so every time the established order changes we unravel another knot. The less knots there are, the weaker the web gets and the stronger we become.
Try to find another one. I'm not sure where it could be, but you should probably look northeast from here, in the June Ruins. I don't know exactly what should happen, but you'll know right away if you are successful in your mission. Another hole will appear in the illusory reality, and your humble servant will use it to pass through.
That is all. I hope we'll meet again soon!
Tep likes to control others' destinies. But that's not the first time you've had to fight against fate, am I right?
Another knot of lies has been unraveled. Soon we will all escape the web of falsehood.
Use this illusion rupture to teleport to the Planar Rim or to another rupture.
Give Che-Lo the Elixir of Memory at Tequatl

Ready! Ready! Here's my tasty magic tea! Look how it seethes, just like in the old days! Now all my neighbors will get their memory back! For years they called me a crazy old man, a fool. This will show them! As coals beget a flame that rises up to the skies, so will the memory of the past be reborn! Go to Che-Lo, give him the tea to drink and listen to him talk!
What's in that cup? What a pleasant aroma! I think I've smelled it somewhere, but I don't recall where...

What... What is this?! Oh heavens! Forgive me, I can't hold back the tears... Oh Ancients, what have we done?!
Yes, I remember now... Everything that used to come to me in obscure visions, knocking on the closed doors of my consciousness. My muddled mind was deaf to them, and only my conscience quietly squeaked: open up, open up...
We were not alone during the dark and dreary era after the Ancients' demise! He was with us the whole time, the spirit of Irdrich, Crocodile Genlun. He is the only reason we didn't perish, or devolve into beasts without language. It was a struggle, but we had learned to survive without the Ancients. And then...
How odd. I barely remember what happened then. There was an explosion, darkness engulfed everything... And then we woke up. Everything was the same as before, but the world around Irdrich was gone, having vanished into this glowing mist. The Immortals lived in the Crystal Palace. We loved them and forgot all about Genlun. How strange!
Old man Che-Go was right this entire time... it's us who were confused... But why?
Make your way to the Tequatl settlement by defeating Tekyans along the way. Defeat 10 Tekyans and War Golem and report to Che-Lo.

What heresy! It has been millennia since outlanders' feet trod on the emerald-green grass of our sacred land! You are as welcome here as a fly on a hot day or a crocodile in a clear river! Death awaits the outlander who disturbs the peace of the Crystal Mountain!
But I can see that you are not afraid! Do you think you are a great warrior? Or do you think that the Tekyan people do not produce strong warriors? Well, just you try to make your way to our settlement, the holy Tequatl! I swear that you won't live longer than a straw hut in a hurricane!
The way to the Crystal Mountain is tough. But will you manage to survive once you've made it?

I can see now - a truly great warrior has come to our land. To defeat the Tekyan Guards and then the Stone Guard singlehandedly... A warrior like that is equal to a tiger or a lion in strength. Verily, a mere mortal could not have achieved this victory alone. The gods of the Crystal Palace themselves must have helped you! And that means your arrival pleases them. Now, tell me: who are you and why did you come to our land?
Question Che-Lo about the Tekyan people
I was told of your arrival. Your reputation as an unequalled warrior precedes you. Tell me about yourself and I will tell you all I can about our people.
I must say that your arrival is a mystery to us. What does the outlander's arrival on the sacred mountain portend for us?
That's the history of our nation and its patrons. Isn't it full of miracles and wonder?
Speak with Che-Ta in the orange grove that's on Sunny Ridge.

Do you want to learn more about the Tekyan people and our Immortal patrons? If you were to ask me which flower truly embodies the soul of the Tekyan people, I wouldn't hesitate with my answer: the orange flower! The color, fragrance and flavor of the orange will tell you all you need to know about us! Go to the orange grove and admire the trees. There you will meet Che-Ta, the grove's guardian. Speak with him: He will tell you more about our people than any sage.
Hey, go easy! Our warriors have already tasted your power! Don't trash our grove as well!
Kill 15 Seedworms in the orange grove on Sunny Ridge and report to Te-Ma.

Some may say that good deeds don't get you anywhere in life, but don't you believe them. Like a fragrant flower, a good person wraps himself in the aroma of his good deeds. Wherever he may go, the word of his good deeds precedes him!
What kind of help do we need? Ah, this dilemma is as old as the garden itself. Perhaps the Immortals are testing us so? Our wonderful trees have been riddled with seedworms for centuries. Large and ferocious, they devour oranges along with branches! Whole generations of gardeners have been exterminating them time after time, but there are always more. If you kill at least fifteen of them, you'll make my life so much easier!
Seedworms have been besieging our grove without respite, like temptations of a sinful world that constantly assail a righteous mind which seeks only enlightenment.

That's fifteen less insects disrupting the peace of our sacred grove and damaging our fragrant trees. Thank you! Remember, any help given to the Tekyan people is not wasted. My people always answer kindness with kindness, and we don't forget favors!
Drive 10 Unholy Tapirs from the orange grove on Sunny Ridge and report to Te-Ma.

We have a problem in our sacred garden - tapirs have become quite fond of it. They are stupid animals with thick skins. You can lecture them for hours about the inviolability of the grove, illuminated by starlight and cleansed by the divine wind... they just keep on chewing through it all. And then they scratch their butts on the sacred trees. What sacrilege! Any such creature ought to be written in as the extra ninth son of the Eight Disrespectful Sons of Tequatl!
Needless to say, this cannot be tolerated. But what can we do? We cannot defile the sacred grove by spilling blood! Killing an insect is one thing, but an animal is quite another story. It's not very divine, either - to kill an animal for being an animal and wanting to eat the most delicious of fruit! So what's the solution?
Here's a special stick. I've spent the whole day making it. It won't break their thick skin, but the animal will still feel the sting of conscience. Beat up on the tapir until he turns his attention to you, then drive him out of the grove with this stick. Could you get rid of a dozen or so, at the very least?
Like a tapir, a fool rushes into the garden, breaking fragile branches without even realizing it... See, there are important lessons to be learned in any situation!
Thanks so much! I fear that they'll just come back tomorrow, but I'll have a new stick ready by then!
Collect 35 Sweet Oranges in the orange grove on Sunny Ridge and take them to Che Kak in Tequatl.

This grove is as old as the Tekyan people themselves. Perhaps it's even older - there are no records of a time when it wasn't here. The orange trees blossomed here after the Ancients' demise, when the whole world around Irdrich disappeared, when the Immortals came to our land... When you touch the bark of these trees, you touch history itself. Stand in their shadow, breathe in the sweet orange aroma, and dwell on the notion of eternity. A notion which describes this grove perfectly.
But I can see that you want to learn about the Immortal patrons of our people. To the south of the grove there is a statue to the greatest of them, the Holy Benefactor. Near the statue you will find Che Kak, who keeps our traditions intact. Collect fresh oranges as a gift for the Benefactor and question Che Kak about the gods. He will be glad to enlighten you.
You want to know about the Benefactor and the Immortals? It's nice to see young people seeking the truth! I'll tell you. Ahem... it's just that my mouth feels very dry, and it's a long story...
Let me have a taste of the fruit you wish to offer the Benefactor. Mmm! Munch-munch-munch... There iff noffing more preffious to the gods than... Munch-munch... Fen fresh oranfes! Yum!
Lay the oranges at the statue's feet and receive the Guardian's blessing.

This is a statue of the Benefactor, leader of the Immortals. When the Tekyan people lived wretched, miserable lives in filth and famine, the Immortals came to us to guide and protect us. They settled in the Crystal Palace on that mountain, from where they showered us with immeasurable bounties. We humbly reciprocate with modest gifts of our own: oranges and incense. But our main offerings are faith, purity and devotion!
Oh, those oranges are so fresh and wonderful! Quickly, place them at the Benefactor's feet!
You look really funny, but the Immortals' generosity extends even to peculiar creatures such as yourself!

How dare you! If the Benefactor sends his servants after you, you must not oppose them or unsheathe your sword. You must humbly accept the fate prepared for you by the Immortals! What terrible heresy! A heretic like you has no place among the righteous Tekyans!
Talk with Te-Ter in the lower reaches of Jumayo River.

Hey, you! You, with the strange fur! Come here, listen to what I say!
Don't listen to Che-Ka. He is crazy! They are all crazy here! Ever since that "benefactor" got here, everyone has gone a bit cookoo!
You have really shown those heretics... Yes, heretics, I know what I said and I stand by it, and Che-Ka can broil with anger if he doesn't like it! The "immortals" are not gods in the slightest; in fact, the creatures that live in the Crystal Palace are plain impostors! And even if all Tekyans lose their minds, I shall never forget...
Heh, you think that I'm some crazy old man, don't you? They all think that. But I can prove to you that I speak the truth, that the true god of the Tekyan people is not this monster!
Go to the lower reaches of Jumayo River. You will find my proof there. There you will meet our true god, the true benefactor of my poor people. Use your own eyes and you will know lies from truth! Look for my grandson Te-Ter, he will tell you everything I taught him. And if he forgets, tell him that I'll whip him to jog his memory!
Did my grandpa send you? Please don't be upset with him. He's old and not quite all there these days. Then, he was always this way...
Collect 3 Sandalwood Sticks and 8 Young Bamboo Shoots in Selva Chetou, sacrifice them to the Tekyan ancestors and receive their answer.

What are you saying! How could we have all died if we are right here, perfectly alive?! Perhaps the Immortals have muddled our minds, but your story about the illusory world just doesn't make any sense.
 Sorry, but no. I've had enough. You can't do this to an old man - more shocks and surprises in one day than over the last half dozen decades! I... I need to think.
Let's do what any righteous Tekyan ought to do in this situation: consult with the ancestors.
To the west of Tequatl, just past Jumayo River, lies Selva Chetou. There you will find an ancient graveyard of the Tekyans. Collect some aromatic sandalwood and tender young bamboo shoots along the way. Sacrifice them at the graveyard, meditate on your offering and wait for the answer.
Our descendants wanted nothing to do with us for so many years... Evidently, they now need something from us!
What a disgusting creature! Is this what my ungrateful descendants have become? Well, can't say I'm surprised! This is what happens when you forget your ancestors!
Collect 8 portions of toad and asp poison by fighting them in the northern part of Selva Chetou and bring them to Sunny Creek in Tequatl.

Look at how brilliantly this world is structured! Nothing is accidental, there is always another side to everything, and then another side, and so on and so forth, ad infinitum! Take, for instance, the swamp in Selva Chetou. At first glance it seems like an impassible quagmire. But if you look a little closer, it is swarming with all sorts of life, albeit much of it isn't sentient: mosquitoes, leeches, toads, snakes... But can you even call that life? A closer look reveals that even the tiniest swamp bug is venomous! But the extraordinary fact is that their venom is used to make the most potent remedies, which extend the lives of Tekyans up to a century!
Now that's something worth contemplating. Even a half hour would be sufficient to attain incredible insights! And when you return, you must share them with me! Oh, and should you decide to collect some venom, be sure to share that as well - there'll always be use for it. However, your primary objective is to contemplate nature!
Asp poison has no color or scent. Toad poison is thick and malodorous. Yet they serve the same purpose!
Oh, thank you! Well, did contemplating the swamp inspire you to new and wonderful insights?
Use Warthog Blood to summon and kill 10 bats. Report to Sunny-Creek in Tequatl.

The senior warriors use lethally dangerous machinery in their search for enlightenment. They dance with Death herself and look for answers in the patterns of Her dance. I never had the courage to do it myself, but perhaps you do?
The ritual is performed as follows. First, you need to find and kill a warthog and collect his blood. Then, sprinkle the blood around yourself. The Emissary of Death, her very incarnation in the form of a bat with leathery wings, will be drawn to the smell. The beast is extremely dangerous, but battling it will allow you to gaze into the depths of your own soul and understand who you are! At least that's what the elder warriors said. Those who perform the ritual ten times and survive are glorified and venerated as great sages in Tequatl. So, are you brave enough?
I am not afraid of land creatures, but bats... Brrrrr, I don't even want to think about them!
Wow! You did it! Tell me, tell me - what did you discover in your dance with Death? No, wait... don't tell me. In fact, don't tell anyone. That is between you and Her.
Kill 15 monkeys in Selva Chetou and return the Ancestor Spirit's Tablet to him.

Are you saying that the Tekyan people were too ashamed to come themselves and sent you instead? Well, they did the right thing! You can't even imagine the thrashing they'd get from me! The shame of it: neglecting your ancestors' graves for so many years, weeds growing on the graves, never burning incense or sacrifice sweet bamboo shoots... Have the Tekyan people utterly lost all sense of piety? Go on, tell me what happened to my foolish tribe?
What are these "Immortals"? Who corrupted them and forced them to worship false gods? Oh, if only I were alive, I'd show them what's what. Oh, there were the times when my glorious name... My name... Erm... Ah...
 Help! My name, my name is lost! My gravestone must have been stolen by monkeys! Outlander, I don't know who you are, but I beg you in the name of the Ancients, in the holy name of Genlun, please get my name from the blasted creatures and return it to the sanctum. What ever would I do without my name? Punish them right and proper so that they wouldn't dream of wreaking mischief in a holy place!
What kind of ancestor would I be without a name? An ordinary ghost, that's all!

There it is, my name, exalted through the ages! Che-Rez! An old sage once said: "If the names are wrong, the words themselves have no foundation. If the words have no foundation, deeds cannot be carried out." You and I have repaired the names, now we can move on to deeds.
Protect Che-Rez' spirit from danger and receive his blessing to fight the Immortals. Report to Che-Lo in Tequatl.
Well, outlander, shall we talk? The wise and powerful Che-Rez is ready to listen to... Holy Genlun's tail, what is that?!
Were you able to speak with the ancestors? I'm ashamed to think what they're saying about us...

The Immortals' minions have attacked the spirit of the honorable Che-Rez, may his name never fade from memory? This proves that we've been praying to false gods this entire time... Oh, the disgrace! What would the Ancients think of us if they were alive... How can we face Genlun now... However, if the ancestors have given us their blessing to fight the false gods, our familial duty demands that we fight!
Complete Tekyan tasks to locate and untangle the illusory web knot near the Crystal Palace.

The better things are, the worse they get. Tep finally figured out what's been going on, and immediately tried to block our access to the illusory world for good. He failed: we have unraveled enough knots so that he's no longer in complete control. I hope that this realization triggered at least one hundredth of the horror that he had been inflicting on every Sarnaut denizen for ages.
Now we are hiding from his legions of mechanized undead in the real world, playing tug o' war, if you will. If Tep regains control over his illusion, we are finished. We must tear the illusory world from his grasp as quickly as we can. And I think I know where we can find the right knot.
Thanks to you, we have discovered that Tep controls the illusion with the help of the Immortals, who dwell in the Crystal Palace. That is where we must look for him. Especially since you've already been blessed by the Tekyan ancestral spirit.
But you had better hurry: all our efforts will be lost if we get devoured by the rusty undead in the real world!
Illusion and reality are drawing ever closer. There is a real war being waged in both worlds, with real victories and defeats.
You are amazing! The web is snapping and unraveling like an old shawl. It's literally hanging on by a thread!
Show the Bone Medallion to Che-Go at Tequatl.

What a wonderful item! It's obviously precious and antique. Truly, the Tekyans have forgotten their history overnight. Everyone of them, except for one strange old man... You should show your find to Che-Go, he will probably recognize it.
Hold on a sec... What have you go there?

Do you even know what this is? I don't believe my eyes! This is an ancient relic which was lost with the arrival of the heretical false gods! Like a fragile flower sprouting on withered soil, a new hope sprouts for the Tekyan people!
Know that this "medallion," as you called it in your ignorance, is actually the Forest Yantra - an ancient symbol of harmony with nature! The Tekyans of ages past meditated on its intricate patterns to attain awareness of their unity with roots and branches. They strolled through the woods immersed in wise and righteous thoughts, without fear of getting lost. When the "immortals" came, monkeys stole this relic from our sanctum. Evidently, wild animals were more deserving of keeping it than we were! But now the relic has been returned! Oh, what blessing! Oh, what fortune!
Test the Forest Yantra on 10 treants on the Selva Chetou and report back to Che-Go in Tequatl.

While the Yantra was stored in our sanctum, we were not afraid of walking trees. Now they attack us as if we are their sworn enemies. We have lost our harmony with nature, lost the connection between flesh and wood. Now that the relic has been restored to us, this harmony should return as well. The treants won't harm anyone who carries the Yantra; they will be like kittens at his feet... That's what I think, anyway. Though I'd rather not be wrong about that.
How about you verify it for me? If the Yantra doesn't work as before, and I take it with me to make peace with the treants, they won't even notice my bones crunching under their feet. You, on the other hand, are used to fighting, so if anything happens you can protect yourself. And if harmony truly has been restored, who better than you to witness the wonders of the recovered relic!

Can we forget about the kittens comment? Just as the sun can develop spots, so does a master orator misspeak at times. But my larger point still stands: if we live in harmony with nature, a treant won't touch a hair on a Tekyan's head!
They rotted? What the deuce! I didn't expect that at all. Does that mean the Yantra now bears a curse instead of harmony? How could that be?
Find Standstill the treant in Selva Chetou, purify the Forest Yantra from defilement, deal with the danger lurking inside and report back to Che-Go in Tequatl.

The Yantra is defiled! Defiled by some wicked heretic! It couldn't have been the Immortals - they don't know enough about our people and secrets. It's painful to even consider this, but it must have been one of us. And I think I know who...
A long time ago, there was an old magician living in Tequatl by the name of Che-Veg. He had devoted his life to seeking the truth, but went too far in his search. He was exiled from Tequatl for indecent words and even less decent actions. I've no doubt that he harbored thoughts of malice and vengeance against his kin...
But that was a long time ago, and Che-Veg is unlikely to still be alive. His wicked legacy, however, remains for us to deal with.
There is a truly ancient treant in the southeastern grove of Selva Chetou. Many years ago he has immersed himself in meditation, and ever since that day he's been virtually indistinguishable from a regular tree. Our people nicknamed him Standstill. His branches radiate purity and wisdom. Lay the Yantra at his roots and ask him to purify it. Only don't go there alone. This ritual is best performed in the company of reliable and righteous companions. I'd say at least 20 of them! The more people gather, the higher the chances that Standstill will hear you!
Why is there so much evil and hatred in a Tekyan soul? How could he defile one of the most ancient relics of his people?

You're telling me that scalawag was still alive? I shudder to think how much hatred he has accumulated in his heart over these long years! I also feel sorry for Standstill... May they both rest in peace, and may the Yantra help them to finally attain harmony within themselves and with the forest.
Collect Honey-sweet Petals, Star apple Berries and pure Spring Water, then bring them to Che-Go in Tequatl.

Isn't it a miracle? Isn't it amazing? Our beloved crocodile has come back to us! He gobbled up the "immortals" like sardines! Rejoice, Tekyans, rejoice! Come on, be happy! Ah...
Look at them! I told you it's they who are crazy, and not I! Jus listen to what they are saying! They... They didn't see anything!
What's up with their forgetfulness? Perhaps something clouded their minds? I can't think of another explanation. Let's try a traditional cure, a magic tea clarifying the memory.
You're not busy with anything important, right? Then go get the ingredients. Here's what I need: honey-sweet petals, star-apple berries, and pure spring water. Got it? Good, now go!
If the tea ceremony helps, I might brew a drink granting common sense next. For the entire village, he he he.
Perfect! But we'll need one other thing to make tea properly...
Kill 14 tigers in the Impassable Wilderness and report to Silk-Thread in Tequatl.

Are you the unbeatable warrior everyone's been talking about? Oh, of course it's you, who else could it be? Forgive me, my head is all screwed up from fear and anger.
Oh, Immortals, what devil crocodile brought me here... And why oh why did I drag my brother with me? I was arrogant, wanted to teach him... And, of course, we had to encounter an entire pride of tigers! Glory to the Benefactor, we managed to escape. But my bro is badly wounded... What if he never walks again? And it's all my fault!
 if you really are a warrior without equal, won't you help me? I have to stay here to take care of my brother, no way I can leave the village. But we can't let a pride of tigers lurk right outside Tequatl, especially not after they've tasted Tekyan blood! Find them and kill them all. I'll find a way to repay you.
Life is unfair: some people play the hero and get whatever they want, while others get into a big fat mess the moment they step foot out the door!
Are there any tigers left around Tequatl? Thank you! Tekyans will never forget you!
Kill Gorger the tiger leader in the Impassable Thicket and report to Silk-Thread in Tequatl.

There must be a reason these tigers have gotten so brazen. Every river has a source, just as every band has a leader. Rumors abound of a tiger in the Impassable Wilderness that's nastier and more aggressive than the whole pride. They say he can swallow three Tekyans whole... but that part is probably untrue: I doubt he can eat more than one at a time. Nevertheless, seeing as the Immortals didn't punish him, we must take matters into our own hands! Perhaps you were sent to us by the Benefactor?
Please, I beg you to destroy the striped bloodsucker. If you do, the entire Tequatl will drink to your health!
Those tigers are real scary! There's something comforting about crocodiles, but those felines... Oh my... I'm rambling again, aren't I?
Thank you! I hope that the monster has been destroyed once and for all. I shudder to think that a new Gorger might be born among the tigers and start terrorizing us common folk all over again!
Find the ruins of a June temple in the Impassable WIlderness, kindle a flame in the chalice and bring a coal to Che-Go in Tequatl.

What do we need to make good tea? Ingredients, water and a saucepan, yes? No! If that's how you mix it, it will just go sour! We need fire! Young people are so thick these days, you have to explain every little thing...
So anyway, we need fire... But not just any old fire, either! Real tea must be made on pure, living flame! There was a time when the Tekyan people kept a flame that had been preserved since the dark ages. That was the flame that warmed us when we lived primal, poverty-stricken lives... But when the "immortals" came, may their eyes and nostrils be filled with thorns, they forced us to extinguish the sacred flame!
Alas, the ancient flame can never be resurrected, but what we can do is kindle a new one. Northeast of here are ruins of a temple of the Ancients. They have overgrown with grass and lianas, so the "immortals" didn't defile the site. Go there and find an altar. Start a fire in the chalice and bring me back a piece of coal. Together we will light a new sacred flame, one that will burn for millennia!
The tears I've shed over the cold ashes of the extinguished flame are immeasurable... Will there ever be cause for joy again?

Oh, what joy! Oh, what bliss! Oh, what countless blessings! I can feel the living warmth of the sacred flame! Quickly, give me the coal and I will kindle a fire. With Genlun's favor, no one will ever extinguish this flame again!
Put to rest 8 Ancient Skeleton Warriors and Leaders and 8 Ancient Skeleton Conjurors in the June Ruins and report to Te-Lo.

An avaricious mind is like a seedworm - it wants only the sweetest fruit and never stops desiring more. The Tekyan people are familiar with the art of magic. Some of it we've learned ourselves, some from the Ancients, and some from the Immortals. Much of it was lost when the Ancients perished, yet there was so much more in this world that even they didn't know! Can you blame a scientist when his inquisitive mind begins to seek the truth off the beaten track?
Argh, whom am I kidding! The truth is that there was an idiot who decided that traditional Tekyan magic wasn't enough, and so he tried his hand in the forbidden art of necromancy. And if that wasn't enough, he did it in the ruins... covered with the ashes of the Ancients! The outcome is before you: the bones of the Ancients rose from the ground and started roaming the land. They might turn up in Tequatl soon! Do I need to tell you who that idiot was? Me!
I beg you now to help me to put the undead to rest before things get worse!
But try to be polite with them as you do it. They are the Ancients, after all... OK, OK, I'll be quiet now.
I swear on the memory of the Ancients, if you manage to deal with the ramifications of my experiments, I will not touch a magic rod ever again! Oh, look, they're crawling out from the ground again!
Search the June Ruins while fighting off the undead and bring Te-Lo the Parchment of Forbidden Knowledge, an inkwell, a magic rod and a censer.

When the ground shifted and I saw bones rise from it, I got scared worse than a rabbit before a pride of tigers! I bolted from there faster than any rabbit! I was in such a hurry that I left all my magical paraphernalia there. Everything that I had worked on for months, left to rot beside the undead... Oh no, don't look at me like that! I am NOT going to experiment with necromancy again, scout's honor!
But then I thought... what if someone else decides to partake of the forbidden knowledge? If that happens, my instruments will bear the harvest of new troubles like some seeds of evil!
Please, collect everything that I've lost and return it to me. I will... erm... destroy them in a special ritual to erase all traces of the magic of death! I will erase my sin as the surf washes away curse words written on the sand!
An inexperienced mage is like a new coffee pot! Both of them are... Erm... Well... No, I guess they're not at all alike. Sorry, I'm much better at magic than public speaking.
There they are! Did anything get damaged? Hurrah, they are as good as new! Yes, yes, I will destroy them all, I promise!
Complete Tekyan tasks to locate and untangle the next knot of the illusory web.

Another knot has been unraveled. This time without pretty explosions in the real world, but don't think Tep is any less frustrated for it. How would I know? Because he's gathering all his forces, both real and illusory. We had no idea he had constructed so many mechanoids! An element of time has been added to our game of chess: every hour brings us one step closer to getting buried under a mountain of rust and dead flesh. So let's hurry and find the next knot. I don't know exactly where it's hidden, but I have a feeling we need to look for it in Tequatl. If Tep doesn't want the Tekyans to remember anything, there must be a reason for that, and that's what we must uncover.
Take this coal to the one who sent you. The old man will know what to do with it.
I wonder how many knots we'll need to break to unravel the entire web? Two, twenty, two hundred? Do we have any chance at all?
Another knot has been broken! But it's too early to break open the champagne - Tep is raising the stakes.
Find Black Bird the scout near the Crystal Mountain

When the dead speak, the living ought to listen with respect. If Che-Rez has blessed us in our war with the Immortals, so be it. It's time to overthrow the false gods and return to the ways of our ancestors.
 There is only one thing I still find troubling: your stories about the illusory world. So many impossible things have happened recently that I really am beginning to question my reality. However, even if all you say is true... Let me ask you - what is reality? If we feel alive in the illusory world, if we feel pain and joy... does that not mean that we are truly alive? You say that our world is but a cogwheel inside some magic machine... but perhaps that machine and your entire "real" world are also insignificant parts of an even larger machine, in an even more "real" reality?
These thoughts are making my head spin, but the takeaway is very simple - remember us! When you fight the Immortals, take care that you don't accidentally destroy our small but precious little world. Don't forget that we still live here.
And now let's get to work. I have already sent our best scout to the Foothills. Her name is Black-Bird. Find her and find out what she was able to learn. May Genlun be with you!

There you are. I already scouted the area - this is going to be a tough job. You can't just stroll into the Crystal Palace. They say that when the Ancients lived in the Palace and Tekyans were welcomed there, the approach was guarded by stone guardians. But since the Immortals moved in, a strange magic that can't even be described in words blocks the way. Only those invited by the Immortals may pass through the mirage... And they will hardly do us that honor, don't you think?
Kill 8 Mantises and 8 Finguses in the Crystal Mountain foothills and report to Gold-Flower.
Wow, I've never heard of such imaginative bugs! Almost as clever as Tekyans! It's scary to have neighbors like that, real scary...
There are no more trained finguses in the forest, right? Yay, Tequatl is saved! Thank you so very, very much!
Kill 14 Rusty Warriors in the Green Foothills and report to Che-Shi.

The Ancients left us an enormous inheritance. We'll never be able to understand most of it, even if ten thousand Tekyans labor over it for ten thousand years. But we did manage to figure out some things and even apply them.
I am the leading expert on the Ancients' technology in all of Tequatl. False modesty aside, I've managed to revive quite a few of their machines. Sometimes these discoveries were useful, but mostly they just confused us... Sometimes we even regretted them. And that's where we are now.
An entire army of war machines is buried in these hills. Some of them we were able to revive and dispatch to guard the borders of our lands from all kinds of pesky creatures. But those dolts roving the hills near along the river? I didn't revive them! It appears that we've accidentally roused a whole army. And the worst part is that they don't obey us!
These are highly efficient war machines we're talking here. If they ever decide to attack Tequatl, that's going to be the end of us. Help us! Break them back down!
So far the most dangerous thing we've found looked like a tea kettle. It killed over a dozen Tekyans and destroyed twice as many houses.
It's such a pity to break the Ancients' gifts. Of course, if these gifts decide to break us, that would be even more of a pity.
Kill the Rusty Field-Marshall in the Green Foothills and report to Che-Shi.

I think I understand why all those war machines have risen and why they don't want to obey us. See, I accidentally roused their commander. He shouted a battle cry - outside of our hearing range, but crystal clear to the sleeping army. That's when the army awoke... It's these kind of discoveries that give me the willies. Why does a general need an army? To start a war. And how many potential enemies are here to war against? Not many at all...
But I think that if we crush the leader, the entire army should disperse, perhaps even fall back to sleep. 'Cause if they don't, then we are all in trouble... It's worth a shot either way.
Of course, you won't be able to do this alone - high-ranking machines are much tougher than regular soldiers. Assemble a team of five friends, that should be enough to handle them.
It's scary to imagine the true military might of the Ancients. It's even scarier to know that it couldn't prevent their demise.

Oh, look at that, I did it! They are no longer marching, but simply meandering from place to place! Let's hope that they'll go to sleep in a couple of days, and we'll be able to dig in their heads some more.
Activate the Logic Machine on the path near the Paradox Veil and survive the Lictor attack. Summon Charles de Doucer using the reality distortion and report your success to him.

My measurements confirm my calculations: this world is trying mightily to reject the paradox, and only the brutal enforcement of the laws of the illusory reality is keeping the veil in place. Nonetheless, the laws of logics remain constant and implacable. And we will use them to banish Tep from his own creation.
 While everyone else was loafing around being useless, I was working on our problem and assembling a logic machine. Go on and activate it somewhere near the veil. The best spot would be at the intersection with the trail going uphill. After some time the paradox that blocks your path will be resolved, and the veil will pop. But do be careful - Tep's servants will sense what's going on and will try to stop you. Don't let them near the machine! This is very, very important! Do whatever you have to, but the logical algorithm must run to completion!
What can I do for you?
Success? Well... That's completely logical... The theory predicted the inevitable... But then why are my hands shaking?
Take measurements in four locations near the Paradox Veil and return to Nomarkh Koses in the Crystal Mountain foothills.

Greetings, pleased to meet you. I heard plenty about you... I was sent here by Charles de Doucer to help you find a passage. The girl briefed me on the situation - not in a particularly scientific way, but she got the gist of it nonetheless. The Crystal Palace is separated from the surrounding world by a barrier I've dubbed the "Paradox Viel." It is a wall made up of the impossible: the final stronghold of Tep, and also his demise, for it is a blatant violation of all existing laws of this world. Presently the force of the paradox helps the web to maintain the illusion, but if it is destroyed, this world will reject its creator with equal force. Do you realize what that means? We are but one step away from victory! But have no doubt - this step will be more difficult than all the others combined.
We'll begin, as always, with research. Take this device - let's call it "reality meter." Take it to the Paradox Veil, take some measurements and, if you survive, bring it back.
Just be careful not to damage it. In our circumstances, it's worth a dozen fighters like you.
If there is anything that can make my embalmed heart happy, it's the results of an experiment supporting my theory. Nice, that's just nice. I think I know how we can tear the Paradox Veil.
Bring 14 pieces of mutton to Alexey Baranov at the Crystal Mountain foothills.

Seeing as we're back in the illusion, why shouldn't we enjoy its benefits? I know, I know - high priority mission, Tep, knots, etc... But I'm sick and tired of chocking on that sorry excuse for food in the real world. Try to imagine what it's like to eat that filth day after day after day! A roasted rat is a delicacy where we're from! The moment I close my eyes, all I see are Kanian pies, tarts, donuts... It's a recipe for madness!
Come on, be a friend and help out! I've seen some sheep in the foothills. Bring me their meat for a barbeque. It's much easier to fight on a full stomach!
Some got so hungry they tried feasting on a necro-mechanoid. May they rest in peace...
Oooh! Fresh meat! Sorry, I felt like a troll for a second there.
Collect 20 juicy fruits in the Crystal Mountain foothills, place them in the trap and report to Black Bird.

They say that every Tekyan has an animal that's his spirit guide. And in the hour of great sorrow or tribulations, one should find their kindred spirit to help find answers to pressing questions. Perhaps that's just a story... But the hour of sorrow and tribulations is upon us - not just me but all Tekyan people. It's a time when even a fairy-tale can offer comfort and hope. I would like to find my spirit animal and ask him for advice. Will you help me?
All the birds on Irdrich are bright and colorful, and only one is black as tar. She soars in the skies above all others. They say that she lives on the very top of the Crystal Mountain. I was named in her honor. Do you think she'll come down from the heavens to speak with me? I've my doubts. But we can try to lure her.
I've made this trap, but we will need bait. I wonder what the bird eats? I like sweet fruit and berries... perhaps she likes them too?
At times I see that bird in the sky and whisper my secrets to her... I wonder if she ever hears me...
I saw her! She is circling in the skies above us... But she doesn't seem to want to fly down here.
Kill 15 parrots in the Crystal Mountain foothills and report to Nomarkh Koses.

In the olden days Zem leaders were turned into mummies upon their death. The internal organs were placed into individual vessels, and the brain was extracted through the nose with a special hook. I am but a humble follower and was not awarded such honor. But whenever I hear the cries of native parrots, I can't help but think that fate was kinder to them. Those blasted birds shriek in the morning, twitter all day, howl in the evening and gossip at night. I can't work under these conditions! I'm not asking you for a spacious lab equipped with cutting-edge magic technology, but a scientist of my caliber ought to be spared this kind of nightmare, don't you agree? Or should I put my research on hold and start chasing parrots through the jungle myself? Is that what you want?!
Why did I ever join this expedition? I'm going to find the moron who told me this would be good for my career... And mummify him.
There, at least some respite. If you ignore the jungle's constant rustling, banging, champing and screeching, it's become almost bearable.
Bring 12 Ginger Roots and 25 Crocodile Tears to Alexey Baranov at the Crystal Mountain foothills.

Meat, meat! Big, raw, juicy pieces of meat! Come to papa... Stop! What are we, goblins? We shouldn't be eating raw meat... Let's barbeque it... Don't look so down, we'll have plenty of time to tear up that web! My people in Kania have a saying: "A war is a war, but don't forget about dinner!"
All right, I'm going to start a fire, while you go look for some herbs. I recall there were some spicy roots growing around here - bring me back a dozen. And salt... we need some salt... Oh, I know! The local crocodiles lunge at everything in sight, but the moment anyone fights back they start crying large crocodile tears. Collect as many of those tears as you can and get back here. We'll cook ourselves a nice meal, treat the Tekyan dame and maybe even that undead nerd... erm... I meant the esteemed Nomarkh Koses. With our bellies full we'll handle Tep with one arm tied behind our backs!
My mom makes the best barbeque in Lightwood. If we survive this - you must come and visit!
Ooh, this is so yummy! And even if it's not real barbeque, who cares?! Bon appétit!
Obtain 14 fish in the Crystal Mountain foothills, put them in the trap and see what happens.

Fruit doesn't appear to interest her. This makes sense: a strong, proud bird like her must be a predator. Shall we try attracting it with meat? Or perhaps fish? Any other ideas?
Then let's try fish. There are some big ones in this river... Crocodiles, obviously, not fish! Kill fifteen or so of them and put them in the trap. Perhaps the bird will like them. And if not, we could try mutton. Or something else entirely!
Caw! Why catch? Want what? Caw!
Find the treasure under the strange stone indicated by the raven and bring it to Black Bird.

Kr-rah!! Little warrior, sister-soul... See. Know. Need help? Quarrrh-rh... Help if let me go!
Find head-stone. More stone around, lots of moss, lots of curl. One stone must turn. What find - answer questions of child-warrior, sister-soul. Also find what help you.
Kharr, now let me go! No life without sky! Kr-caw!
Black Bird spoke to you? Without me? Argh, my rotten luck... Alas...

This is ancient! In fact, it's the Ancients' handiwork! But why did the black bird say that this treasure will give me answers?
Thank you. Could I keep this for a while? I need to think. The prophetic bird doesn't caw for nothing.
Escort Gold-Flower through the thicket of the forest.

Sh-h-h! I'm hiding! Don't speak so loud, you will attract predators!
What? You're not afraid of predators? Really, like, not at all? Then maybe you could walk me home? Because I'm... Well... just a little bit... Lost.
Wow, there are some brave souls out there... Me, I'm afraid of everything.
Thank you, thank you! I thought I was going to die. Enough scares to last me a year!
Ascend the Crystal Mountain after defeating Crystal Guards with the Spear of Truth.

That's it. The hard part is behind us, and the path to the center of the illusion is clear. All you have to do is ascend to the Temple and unravel the last knot. It's being guarded by crystal guards, but you aren't afraid of them, are you? You wield a spear that kills even Lictors; I'm sure crystals won't give you any trouble. Victory! Onward!
Is the way to the Crystal Mountain clear? So what are you waiting for? Hurry up and destroy the false gods!
How could this happen? The legends lied... What are we to do now?
Obtain 10 Magic Essences by fighting fire elementals on the Crystal Mountain. Then reforge the fragments of the spear and the ancient sword into a new sword and report to Black-Bird.

You know, I thought about things and remembered something. I was wrong! There was something like this in the legends! Do you remember "Dreams in the Amethyst Pavilion"? Oh, of course you don't, sorry. I have all the scrolls - if you sit down to read them, you won't be able to stop!
So anyway, in the fifth dream Che-Sten becomes so powerful that he dares to challenge the gods themselves. He descends into the depths of the Crystal Mountain, to its very heart, and forges a sword in its flames. He tempers the sword with the essence of magic and binds a living soul to it. Then he ascends the Crystal Mountain, mowing over the crystal guards as he does. Stunned by his power, the Immortals accept him as one of their own, then shroud the mountain with a veil... Wait a second - if the Immortals are evil, does that mean Che-Sten is evil as well? Or maybe they didn't really take him in? I'm scared to even consider the possibility...
Nevertheless, we must try. I know where to find the cave where Che-Sten forged his sword. The magic spirits that provided the essence of magic for his sword still live there. You already have a weapon with a bound living soul, albeit a broken one. The Black-Bird spoke of the old sword of the Ancients. You can forge a new sword out of it in the flames of the mountain, just like in the times of old.
You must think of a name for your sword. Something pretty that will sound good in legends. Crystalsmash? Or Shatterglass? Or Crystalrupture? Go on. I'll think of a few more names in the meantime.
An ancient sword has been reforged, and a new hero ascends the Crystal Mountain... It's a pity there's no scribe in Tequatl good enough to pen a new legend! Maybe I should try...
Fight your way to the top of the Crystal Mountain and depose the false gods.

Before you arrived we groveled before the Immortals and didn't even suspect that they were lying to us. Now the whole village will pray for you and your victory! Don't let us down, for if you fail, not even Genlun will save us from the wrath of the false gods.
Good luck! Go and create a new legend with this sword!
The veil has been broken, and you now have a reborn sword. Now go! Cast the impostors from the mountain and into the abyss!
Is that... it? There are no more Immortals?

Our lives until now have been a dream, a nightmare. We didn't remember our own past and worshipped a grandiose lie. Awakening has been painful, yet it's still better than living a lie. However, there is one secret I will ask you to keep to yourself: the truth about the real world, that we are all actually dead and living in an illusion... My people don't need to know that. Unlike you, we don't have bodies in the real world, and this "truth" would bring nothing but senseless sorrow to the Tekyan people. We will live, raise our children and write legends about your heroic deeds. And maybe someday your sages will find a way to transfer us from illusion into reality.
But in the meantime we will revel in the fruits of Irdrich - they taste real enough! Today all of Tequatl celebrates your achievements and our history reborn. I understand that you are in a hurry, but you must celebrate with us - we won't take no for an answer! Look, fireworks are about to begin!
It's been a while since we had a reason to enjoy fireworks. Hey, maybe we should make today an annual holiday?

The celebration is over. But a new chapter for the Tekyan people is just beginning. I don't know what it's going to be like. But there's one thing I do know - there won't be any room in it for masters or lords!
Return to the real world and speak with Klavdia Kalugina.

That's it. It's time for you to return to your own world and fight those who revived us... Isn't it funny - they revived us only to take away our memories and turn us into slaves! Come visit us if you find the time - you are always welcome in Tequatl. And don't forget us. After all, forgetfulness is the true death.
Have you freed the center of the illusion? All right... But it's too late. I'm not sure that we will have the chance to enjoy this victory.
Kill Patsuk the giant rat near Tequatl and report to Che-Ta.

Nothing in our world exists without reason. Any tree or animal or even the smallest insect can teach an inquisitive mind a valuable lesson. Some creatures teach us wisdom, others can show a fighter how to handle a weapons and his own body... And then there are those who set the opposite example, one of villainy. Their purpose is to help us find the evil in our hearts and uproot it!
One such creature has been spotted outside Tequatl. It's a disgusting gray rat the size of a tapir! The creature sneaks into the sacred grove at night and gnaws on the sacred trees! And if that's not enough: like a fetid wound that festers unless cleaned, this rat has bred an entire pack of creatures in its own image. If the young rats are allowed to mature, they will be a danger to even the great Tree! Please help rid Tequatl of this plague! Gather friends who are as mighty as you and destroy the vile monster! And don't forget to reflect on the nature of good and evil.
Scientists claim that rats are born like any other creatures, but the ancient books say that they emerge from filth and decay. Perhaps that's how this rat was born, too?
And thus good triumphed over evil. Would you like to sit down with your friends in the shade of an orange tree and meditate on the true nature of your victory?
Descend to the bottom of the gorge and speak with the members of the expedition.

So you want learn about Marai-Nui, cursed Crystal-Mount? Kha! Even though you have no wings, you are brave! Kh-khar-r-r, quarr, grrrrreat. I'll tell you what I saw.
Elders said long ago, no one could fly to Marai-Nui, taboo. But when did youngsters ever listen to elders? We were six... A sharp sword in the paw, a strong armor on the body, a mighty amulet on the chest, a wind in the head! We flew across the gorge... There were scary statues there. Walking statues! We six barely won over one, cast into gorge and fell in ourselves. My friends died, I lost a wing... Everyone says, I've lost my mind as well...
Do you want to go there? Kha-quarr, you're brave. You cannot go without wings... Children of the Wind won't help you. Maybe you should ask help from other wingless? Yes, yes, you're not the first to ask me about the Crystal Mountain. Other wingless also asked questions and went down into the gorge. Go look for them. Perhaps they have find the road?

Oh, I'm so glad to see you! Help, at last! As you can see, the League and the Empire find themselves in the same boat again, metaphorically speaking. But why does this always happen when the stupid allegorical boat is about to sink?!
Question Sookie Dry-Wing, Shorr Fly-by-Shore and Zuu Addle-Pate about the mountain in the north. Report to Yasskul Tikhti at the Imperial Outpost.

Finally. I was afraid that someone got you on the way here. We must be very careful now - Tep has already sensed serious danger, and victory is still only a distant hope.
We've combed through the entire Pearl Ring and the Windy Hills. The center of the illusion isn't there, that's for certain. That leaves only one place: the mountain in the north. We haven't found a way to get there, though. The islands are separated by a deep abyss. Even squawkers steer clear of the place, and the aviaks... They are too scared to talk. No matter how much we questioned them, they wouldn't divulge any useful information.
Now, I understand that you've earned their respect. Try questioning them. If they don't open their beaks to you, then we'll have to consider telepathic intervention.
Well, are the aviaks talking or do we need to start using more persuasive methods?
Taboo... Well, at least they gave us one clue.
Find Ulumi Half-Wing in the Muggy Jungle and ask him about the Crystal Mountain.

That means some aviaks have been there. Our next step seems quite obvious. I've seen this Ulumi. He's covered in dirt, you can't even tell the color of his wings. His eyes are mad, he's always talking to himself... It's a sad sight. Even though he's gone mad, I hope the old boy remembers something about his trip to the Crystal Mountain. And if he doesn't... well, I think there was a decent psychiatrist in the expedition team...
Who are you? You've come to laugh at an old cripple? Cough, cough... Ha! Look at yourself: you don't have any wings! Ha ha ha... Kha-khrr...
Who attacked? Ulumi attacked? Who's crazy here, Ulumi or you wingless? Kharr... There was no fight!
